cs.t: My washer and dryer have non-tactile keys that require long-presses.  Same for the oven.  Fridge has an LED screen that lights up the kitchen at night (why?). Also non-tactile.  Over time I find myself pressing my body-weight into the buttons. Also small appliances like pressure cookers, air-friers have gaudy LEDs with non-tactile buttons, and irritating charms. Now for a positive example: my italian Gaggia Espresso machine : 3 large rocker switches and 2 status LEDs.  It could easily be operated by touch alone.  And I expect it to last 30 years with adequate maintenance. And besides the mechanism, no extraneous noises whatsoever.
cs.th: The Windows 11 taskbar is an annoying step backward
